candidate_relations.reason: Sweet syndrome and acute febrile neutrophilic dermatosis are established synonyms for the same condition. The clinical record supports this diagnosis: abrupt-onset painful/asymptomatic neutrophilic plaques with central pseudovesiculation, dense dermal neutrophilic infiltrate without vasculitis on biopsy, peripheral leukocytosis with neutrophilia, and absence of alternative explanations. The candidate label explicitly names both the eponym and the descriptive synonym, fully capturing the reference diagnosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Sweet syndrome (acute febrile neutrophilic dermatosis) is the full diagnostic entity matching the reference

case_quality_flags: Classic Sweet syndrome presentation but notably afebrile and asymptomatic, which is atypical; however, afebrile cases are recognized and do not exclude the diagnosis
Bence-Jones protein testing and abdominal imaging suggest workup for malignancy-associated Sweet syndrome, though no malignancy was identified
